newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Grande takes over loss-making Nakamichi.
newsitem.headline: Grande takes over loss-making Nakamichi.

text.p: Grande Holdings Ltd announced on Monday it would acquire a 70 pct interest in Tokyo-listed, loss-making Nakamichi Corporation.

In the first part of a two-part agreement, Grande said on November 20 it would sell its 60 percent holding in Hong Kong-based Lafe International Holdings Ltd to Nakamichi for a total of HK$2.201 billion to Nakamichi.
In the second part of the deal, Nakamichi would issue 64 million new shares to Grande for a total subscription price of HK$2.428 billion.
Lafe said in an announcement published on Monday the shortfall of HK$227.7 million would be funded from internal resources.
After the issue of new shares, Grande will hold a 70 percent stake in the enlarged issued capital of Nakamichi.
Grande will not be required to make a general offer for Nakamichi under Japanese regulations.

The net proceeds of the subscriptions of HK$227.7 million will not be available for the repayment of indebtedness to the major bankers of Nakamichi. The HK$227.7 million is payable on or before 16 January, the announcement said.

The issue price of the subscription shares of 550 Japanese yen (HK$38 per share) represents a discount of about 10 percent to the average closing prices of the Nakamichi for the six months ended November 19, it said.

Nakamichi is principally engaged in the design and manufacture of audio products as well as computer peripherals. The company reported losses (after tax) of HK$89 million in 1995 and HK$260 million in 1996.
Lafe is a manufacturer of computer components, chiefly computer magnetic heads which are manufactured in China and distributed worldwide.
Trading in the shares of Grande, which was suspended on November 22, is expected to resume on November 25.
